items.q: Yeah, he came to me and he said, “I’d like to have you with JATP,”

ctx.x: Yeah, he came to me and he said, “I’d like to have you with JATP,” and I was a wise guy. I said something like, “I don’t want to be part of your circus” or something. You know how young people are.

items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: This is funny because Norman decided that since so much time had passed, he decided to title this “Buddy DeFranco meets the Oscar Peterson Quartet.”

ctx.x: This is funny because Norman decided that since so much time had passed, he decided to title this “Buddy DeFranco meets the Oscar Peterson Quartet.” When we actually met in the 50s and played together at the Jazz at the Philharmonic. Night after night. And recorded several albums before together, including one of my favorites, the “George Gershwin Songbook.” Russ Garcia arrangements, the big orchestra, that’s one of the nicest. But this was fun. It’s always fun to work with Oscar. Always. Because he’s so dynamic…
Interesting statement. How to play for the clarinet.
